rationale: SGA-to-FGA switch from aripiprazole. Pharmacologically notable: aripiprazole is a D2 partial agonist, while haloperidol is a full D2 antagonist. As haloperidol builds and displaces aripiprazole at D2 receptors, the activation and energy effects of aripiprazole will diminish — this is usually welcome in patients with aripiprazole-induced agitation or akathisia. The reverse transition (akathisia improving) should be monitored. Aripiprazole's very long half-life (~75h) means it provides a natural slow washout. Baseline ECG mandatory for haloperidol. Metabolic parameters: aripiprazole is metabolically neutral; haloperidol is also low metabolic risk — no significant change expected. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start haloperidol 2 mg. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg. Baseline ECG mandatory. Akathisia from aripiprazole should begin to resolve as full D2 antagonism increases.
Increase haloperidol to 5 mg target. Plateau aripiprazole — its long half-life means taper can be gentle.
Begin reducing aripiprazole to 10 mg. Haloperidol at steady state. Assess for haloperidol-induced EPS — have benzhexol available.
Reduce aripiprazole to 5 mg. Haloperidol dominant. Aripiprazole still present due to long half-life — minimal rebound expected.
Stop aripiprazole. Continue haloperidol 5 mg. Recheck QTc at haloperidol steady state. Monitor for haloperidol EPS burden.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: aripiprazole 15 mg ≈ haloperidol 5 mg (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
